## Context / Problem
During a compaction fold, `_build_authorship_ledger` -> `authorship.identify_signer` -> `_keyring_for` -> `rebar.show_ticket` -> `ensure_fresh` ran while `_compact_locked` held the store write lock. When the 60 s freshness marker had expired, `ensure_fresh` ran `git fetch` (network in production) and then `sync.reconverge`, which requested the same store write lock the fold already held, waited out its 2 s pass against its own process, and gave up.

Measured on a clone of `tickets` at `daa3a65239b^` with a local mirror as `origin` (2026-11-03, `origin/main` `25bce6c0550`): first signed fold `ensure_fresh` 2.22 s, nested lock wait 2.04 s, fetch 0.11 s (local mirror; production fetches over the network). Evidence on `breezelike-travelsick-moray`.

## Approach
Delivered by the same change as `breezelike-travelsick-moray` (Gerrit 3269), which follows the compute-before-lock pattern of `finalize_event` and `preresolve_unmapped_positions`:
1. `compact_txn.preresolve_signers` resolves each signed event's verifying key BEFORE `lock.acquire`; `_build_authorship_ledger(..., signers=...)` uses the map and looks up only a key it misses.
2. The locked fold body runs under `ticket_reads.local_read_context()`, so no read inside the lock fetches or calls `sync.reconverge`.
The same commit also passes pre-resolved attribution to `compact_plan.build_snapshot_event` and installs the stderr handler in `compact_trigger.run_sweep` for the parent bug's timing line.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py`: `preresolve_signers`, signer map in `_build_authorship_ledger`, locked body under `local_read_context`.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_plan.py`: optional `attribution` on `build_snapshot_event` (same commit).
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact_trigger.py`: stderr handler in `run_sweep` (same commit).
- `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`: lock-state probes.

## Testing
Each probe records whether the store lock dir exists at the call (state, not duration). A test with a bare remote and an expired freshness throttle observes `sync._coordinated_fetch`, `sync.reconverge` and `lock.acquire`; on the old code all three ran under the lock. Ledger equality is compared with and without the pre-resolved map, and a map missing one key still yields that event's signer with exactly one lookup.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A fold with signed events runs no `git fetch` and no store-lock acquisition while `_compact_locked` holds the lock (test observes the lock dir at each call: `test_no_fetch_or_nested_lock_request_while_the_fold_holds_the_lock` in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`).
- [x] The authorship ledger is unchanged for the same input (`test_presolved_signers_leave_the_ledger_unchanged` in `tests/unit/test_compact_fold_prelock.py`).
